17|# "delete" explicitly for deployments whose backing filesystem is not WAL
18|# crash-safe, such as Linux containers bind-mounted through macOS virtiofs,
19|# NFS, or SMB. Hermes will not live-downgrade a database already open in WAL.
20|database:
21|  journal_mode: "wal"  # Supported values: "wal", "delete"
22|  # Optional WAL sizing pragmas (integers). Unset = SQLite defaults.
23|  # wal_autocheckpoint: 1000     # pages between automatic checkpoints
24|  # journal_size_limit: 67108864 # cap the WAL/journal file size in bytes
25|  #
26|  # Durability level for every state.db connection: OFF, NORMAL, FULL, EXTRA
27|  # (or 0-3). Unset leaves SQLite's default, which is baked in at compile time
28|  # (SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_SYNCHRONOUS) and therefore differs between the bundled
29|  # interpreter, a distro python3 and a Homebrew one. Set it if you need to
30|  # know which one you are running rather than infer it. On macOS this is a
31|  # floor, not a pin: values below FULL are refused because Darwin's fsync()
32|  # does not guarantee write ordering, while EXTRA is honored normally.
33|  # synchronous: FULL

39|# this value when the operating system permits it. The value is clamped to the

119|  # broken (e.g. vLLM with --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml + a reasoning parser
120|  # can leak tool calls into plain text instead of returning tool_calls —
121|  # #72901). Orthogonal to display.streaming, which controls token rendering
122|  # only.
123|  # streaming: true

126|  # provider: "azure-foundry"
127|  # base_url: "https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1"
128|  # auth_mode: "entra_id"      # DefaultAzureCredential: az login, managed identity, workload identity, etc.
129|  # default: "gpt-4o"          # Deployment/model name

131|  #   scope: "https://ai.azure.com/.default"  # Optional; this is the default.

133|  # ── Token limits — two settings, easy to confuse ──────────────────────────
134|  #
135|  # context_length: TOTAL context window (input + output tokens combined).
136|  #   Controls when Hermes compresses history and validates requests.
137|  #   Leave unset — Hermes auto-detects the correct value from the provider.
138|  #   Set manually only when auto-detection is wrong (e.g. a local server with
139|  #   a custom num_ctx, or a proxy that doesn't expose /v1/models).
140|  #
141|  # context_length: 131072
142|  #
143|  # ollama_num_ctx: Ollama only — the num_ctx sent on every chat request.
144|  #   Hermes auto-detects the model's window and sends it (Ollama otherwise
145|  #   defaults to 2048); context_length, if set, caps the detected value.
146|  #   An explicit ollama_num_ctx is sent as-is (never capped) — set it to
147|  #   pin VRAM use.
148|  #
149|  # ollama_num_ctx: 32768
150|  #
151|  # Output-token limits are provider-owned, not user configuration. Native
152|  # protocols requiring a limit receive an internal value from Hermes.
153|
154|  # ── Custom request headers (optional) ─────────────────────────────────────
155|  #
156|  # default_headers: extra HTTP headers sent on every request to an
157|  #   OpenAI-compatible endpoint. User values take precedence over the
158|  #   provider/SDK defaults, so this is the supported way to override the
159|  #   OpenAI Python SDK's identifying headers (User-Agent: OpenAI/Python ...,
160|  #   X-Stainless-*) when a custom provider sits behind a gateway/WAF that
161|  #   rejects them — e.g. an upstream that returns "502 Upstream access
162|  #   forbidden" for the SDK default User-Agent but accepts a plain one.
163|  #   Applies on the OpenAI wire only (not native Anthropic / Bedrock).
164|  #
165|  # default_headers:
166|  #   User-Agent: "curl/8.7.1"
167|  #
168|  # extra_headers: accepted as an alias of default_headers (merged, with
169|  #   extra_headers winning when both are set) — matches the per-provider
170|  #   extra_headers key below.
171|  #
172|  # Per-provider variant: named providers / custom_providers entries accept an
173|  # extra_headers dict scoped to that endpoint only — for reverse proxies,
174|  # gateways, or custom auth (e.g. Cloudflare Access service tokens).
175|  # Merged onto SDK/provider defaults with the entry's values winning.
176|  # Header values are treated as secrets and are never logged.
177|  #
178|  # providers:
179|  #   my-proxy:
180|  #     base_url: "https://llm.internal.example.com/v1"
181|  #     key_env: "MY_PROXY_API_KEY"
182|  #     extra_headers:
183|  #       CF-Access-Client-Id: "xxxx.access"
184|  #       CF-Access-Client-Secret: "${CF_ACCESS_SECRET}"
185|  #       X-Client-Name: "hermes-agent"
186|  #
187|  # session_affinity_header: NAME of a header that carries Hermes' conversation
188|  # id on every request to that provider (all api_modes + auxiliary calls). Off
189|  # unless set. For session-aware proxies that otherwise treat each agent-loop
190|  # request as a new conversation and replay the whole history upstream.
191|  #
192|  # providers:
193|  #   my-proxy:
194|  #     base_url: "http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1"
195|  #     session_affinity_header: x-litellm-session-id
196|# providers:
197|#   meta:
198|#     base_url: https://api.meta.ai/v1
199|#     api_key: ${MODEL_API_KEY}
200|#     # api_mode auto-detected as codex_responses for api.meta.ai; no need to set
201|#     # (the bundled meta-ai provider covers this — a named custom provider is
202|#     # only needed for a non-default Meta-compatible endpoint)
203|# Fast/priority tier behind an OpenAI-compatible gateway or proxy: agent.service_tier
204|# (`/fast`) only reaches first-party endpoints; ask a gateway for its own tier via
205|# extra_body, which is merged into every request routed to that provider.
206|# providers:
207|#   my-gateway:
208|#     base_url: https://gateway.example.com/v1
209|#     api_key: ${MY_GATEWAY_KEY}
210|#     extra_body:
211|#       service_tier: priority   # whatever tier value your gateway documents
212|# providers:
213|#   router:
214|#     base_url: https://api.router.com/v1
215|#     api_key: ${RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY}
216|#     # api_mode auto-detected as codex_responses for api.router.com — the
217|#     # Responses API is Router's native wire (chat/completions is only a
218|#     # compatibility shim). The bundled router provider covers this; a named
219|#     # custom provider is only needed for a non-default Router-compatible
220|#     # endpoint.
221|
222|
223|# Command-minted credentials (optional): key_cmd
224|# ------------------------------------------------------------------
225|# Enterprise gateways often issue SHORT-LIVED bearers (SSO/OIDC brokers, cloud
226|# IAM, internal auth proxies) rather than static API keys, so a value copied
227|# into .env via `key_env` is stale within the hour and every later request 401s.
228|# `key_cmd` names a command that PRINTS a token instead: Hermes runs it per
229|# request (cached until shortly before expiry), so long sessions keep working
230|# with no restart.
231|#
232|# Contract: print ONLY the token on stdout, either bare or as JSON with an
233|# "access_token" field ("expires_in" is honoured). Same shape as OAuth 2.0
234|# token endpoints, Claude Code's `apiKeyHelper`, `gcloud auth
235|# print-access-token`, and `aws ecr get-login-password`.
236|#
237|# Precedence: an explicit --api-key still wins; otherwise key_cmd is preferred
238|# over inline api_key / key_env on that entry.
239|#
240|# Applies to the main agent turn and to auxiliary tasks (title generation,
241|# context compression, vision, embedding) alike.
242|#
243|# Not to be confused with `secrets.command`, which is a different mechanism:
244|# that one runs a helper ONCE at startup to populate env vars for many secrets
245|# at the process level. Use it for a vault or keychain helper that hands back a
246|# KEY=VALUE blob. Use `key_cmd` when ONE provider needs a credential refreshed
247|# DURING a session, because a startup-time env var cannot be re-minted after it
248|# expires.
249|#
250|# providers:
251|#   my-gateway:
252|#     base_url: "https://gateway.internal.example.com/v1"
253|#     api_mode: chat_completions
254|#     key_cmd: "my-auth-cli print-token --profile prod"
255|#
256|# Worked example — an AI gateway that routes by model family, so one entry per
257|# wire format shares the same credential helper:
258|#
259|# providers:
260|#   dbx:                             # OpenAI-compatible (MLflow) route
261|#     base_url: "https://<workspace>.cloud.databricks.com/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1"
262|#     api_mode: chat_completions
263|#     model: databricks-claude-sonnet-4-6
264|#     key_cmd: "databricks auth token -p MY-PROFILE"
265|#   dbx-gpt:                         # OpenAI Responses route
266|#     base_url: "https://<workspace>.cloud.databricks.com/ai-gateway/openai/v1"
267|#     api_mode: codex_responses
268|#     model: databricks-gpt-5-5
269|#     key_cmd: "databricks auth token -p MY-PROFILE"
270|#   dbx-claude:                      # Anthropic Messages route
271|#     base_url: "https://<workspace>.cloud.databricks.com/ai-gateway/anthropic"
272|#     api_mode: anthropic_messages
273|#     model: databricks-claude-fable-5
274|#     key_cmd: "databricks auth token -p MY-PROFILE"
275|
276|# Named provider overrides (optional)
277|# Use this for per-provider request timeouts, non-stream stale timeouts,
278|# and per-model exceptions.
279|# Applies to the primary turn client on every api_mode (OpenAI-wire, native
280|# Anthropic, and Anthropic-compatible providers), the fallback chain, and
281|# client rebuilds during credential rotation.  For OpenAI-wire chat
282|# completions (streaming and non-streaming) the configured value is also
283|# used as the per-request ``timeout=`` kwarg so it wins over the legacy
284|# HERMES_API_TIMEOUT env var (which still applies when no config is set).
285|# ``stale_timeout_seconds`` controls the non-streaming stale-call detector and
286|# wins over the legacy HERMES_API_CALL_STALE_TIMEOUT env var. Leaving these
287|# unset keeps the legacy defaults (HERMES_API_TIMEOUT=1800s,
288|# HERMES_API_CALL_STALE_TIMEOUT=90s, native Anthropic 900s). The
289|# implicit non-stream stale detector is auto-disabled for local endpoints
290|# and can scale upward for very large contexts.
291|#
292|# Not currently wired for AWS Bedrock (bedrock_converse + AnthropicBedrock
293|# SDK paths) — those use boto3 with its own timeout configuration.
294|#
295|# providers:
296|#   ollama-local:
297|#     request_timeout_seconds: 300   # Longer timeout for local cold-starts
298|#     stale_timeout_seconds: 900     # Explicitly re-enable stale detection on local endpoints
299|#   anthropic:
300|#     request_timeout_seconds: 30    # Fast-fail cloud requests
301|#     models:
302|#       claude-opus-4.6:
303|#         timeout_seconds: 600       # Longer timeout for extended-thinking Opus calls
304|#   openai-codex:
305|#     models:
306|#       gpt-5.4:
307|#         stale_timeout_seconds: 1800  # Longer non-stream stale timeout for slow large-context turns
308|
309|# =============================================================================
310|# Unified Timeouts (operation deadlines)
311|# =============================================================================
312|# One place to override Hermes's internal operation deadlines (seconds).
313|# Keys are dotted paths resolved by agent/deadline.py:resolve_timeout().
314|# Precedence: this section > legacy HERMES_* env var (back-compat) > built-in
315|# default. 0 or a negative value disables the bound (unbounded); very large
316|# values are clamped to a platform-safe maximum automatically.
317|#
318|# Currently resolved keys (more paths migrate here over time — see issue #85125):
319|#
320|# timeouts:
321|#   tools:
322|#     concurrent_batch: 420   # Deadline for a parallel tool-call batch
323|#                             # (legacy env: HERMES_CONCURRENT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_S)
324|#     sequential_call: 420    # Deadline for one sequentially-executed tool call.
325|#                             # Defaults to concurrent_batch's value so the two
326|#                             # executor paths stay in sync; human waits
327|#                             # (approval prompts, clarify) never count against it.
328|
329|# =============================================================================
330|# OpenRouter Provider Routing (only applies when using OpenRouter)
331|# =============================================================================
332|# Control how requests are routed across providers on OpenRouter.
333|# See: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection
334|#
335|# provider_routing:
336|#   # Sort strategy: "price" (default), "throughput", or "latency"
337|#   # Append :nitro to model name for a shortcut to throughput sorting.
338|#   sort: "throughput"
339|#
340|#   # Only allow these providers (provider slugs from OpenRouter)
341|#   # only: ["anthropic", "google"]
342|#
343|#   # Skip these providers entirely
344|#   # ignore: ["deepinfra", "fireworks"]
345|#
346|#   # Try providers in this order (overrides default load balancing)
347|#   # order: ["anthropic", "google", "together"]
348|#
349|#   # Require providers to support all parameters in your request
350|#   # require_parameters: true
351|#
352|#   # Data policy: "allow" (default) or "deny" to exclude providers that may store data
353|#   # data_collection: "deny"
354|#
355|#   # Per-model overrides: same keys, applied only when the agent is on that model
356|#   # (spelling-tolerant match; unset keys fall through to the flat values above).
357|#   # models:
358|#   #   "openai/gpt-6-astra":
359|#   #     only: ["openai"]
360|#   #   "anthropic/claude-fable-5.1":
361|#   #     only: ["anthropic"]
362|
363|# =============================================================================
364|# OpenRouter Response Caching (only applies when using OpenRouter)
365|# =============================================================================
366|# Cache identical API responses at the OpenRouter edge for free instant replays.
367|# When enabled, identical requests (same model, messages, parameters) return
368|# cached responses with zero billing. Separate from Anthropic prompt caching.
369|# See: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/response-caching
370|#
371|# openrouter:
372|#   response_cache: true         # Enable response caching (default: true)
373|#   response_cache_ttl: 300      # Cache TTL in seconds, 1-86400 (default: 300)
374|
375|# =============================================================================
376|# Git Worktree Isolation
377|# =============================================================================
378|# When enabled, each CLI session creates an isolated git worktree so multiple
379|# agents can work on the same repo concurrently without file collisions.
380|# Equivalent to always passing --worktree / -w on the command line.
381|#
382|# worktree: true    # Always create a worktree when in a git repo
383|# worktree: false   # Default — only create when -w flag is passed
384|#
385|# By default a new worktree branches from the freshly-fetched remote tip
386|# (the current branch's upstream, else the remote's default branch) so it
387|# starts current with the project instead of from the local clone's
388|# (possibly stale) HEAD. Set worktree_sync: false to branch from local HEAD
389|# instead — useful when offline or when you deliberately want the clone's
390|# exact current state as the base.
391|#
392|# worktree_sync: true   # Default — branch from the fetched remote tip
393|# worktree_sync: false  # Branch from local HEAD (offline / pinned base)
394|
395|# =============================================================================
396|# Kanban Review Dispatch
397|# =============================================================================
398|# First-class review tasks are dispatched automatically by default. The worker
399|# is spawned with the bundled sdlc-review skill and can approve, request changes
400|# back to the original implementer, or escalate a genuine external blocker.
401|# Disable this only when every review is performed manually from the dashboard.
402|  api_mode: chat_completions
403|kanban:
404|  review_dispatch: true

406|# =============================================================================
407|# Terminal Tool Configuration
408|# =============================================================================
409|# Choose ONE of the following terminal configurations by uncommenting it.
410|# The terminal tool executes commands in the specified environment.
411|
412|# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
413|# OPTION 1: Local execution (default)
414|# Commands run directly on your machine in the current directory
415|# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
416|# Working directory behavior:
417|#   - CLI (`hermes` command): Uses "." (current directory where you run hermes)
418|#   - Gateway/messaging/cron: Uses terminal.cwd here; legacy .env cwd values are deprecated
419|cron:
420|  catch_up_missed: true  # False skips past-grace recurring misses after planned downtime.
421|
422|terminal:
423|  backend: "local"
424|  cwd: "."  # For local backend: "." = current directory. Ignored for remote backends unless a backend documents otherwise.
425|  # Desktop xterm font. Install the font locally; Nerd Fonts render Powerlevel10k glyphs.
426|  # font_family: "MesloLGS NF"  # Also accepts a CSS stack; blank uses bundled JetBrains Mono.
427|  timeout: 180
428|  # HOME policy for tool subprocesses:
429|  #   auto    - default: host uses your real HOME; containers use HERMES_HOME/home
430|  #   real    - force your real OS-user HOME
431|  #   profile - force HERMES_HOME/home for strict per-profile CLI config isolation
432|  home_mode: "auto"
433|  docker_mount_cwd_to_workspace: false  # SECURITY: off by default. Opt in to mount the launch cwd into Docker /workspace.
434|  lifetime_seconds: 300
435|  # sudo_password: "hunter2"  # Optional: pipe a sudo password via sudo -S. SECURITY WARNING: plaintext.
436|  # sudo_password: ""         # Explicit empty password: try empty and never open the interactive sudo prompt.
437|
438|# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
439|# OPTION 2: SSH remote execution
440|# Commands run on a remote server - agent code stays local (sandboxed)
441|# Great for: keeping agent isolated from its own code, using powerful remote hardware
442|# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
443|# terminal:
444|#   backend: "ssh"
445|#   cwd: "/home/myuser/project"  # Path on the REMOTE server
446|#   timeout: 180
447|#   lifetime_seconds: 300
448|#   ssh_host: "my-server.example.com"
449|#   ssh_user: "myuser"
450|#   ssh_port: 22
451|#   ssh_key: "~/.ssh/id_rsa"  # Optional - uses ssh-agent if not specified
452|
453|# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
454|# OPTION 3: Docker container
455|# Commands run in an isolated Docker container
456|# Great for: reproducible environments, testing, isolation
457|# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
458|# terminal:
459|#   backend: "docker"
460|#   cwd: "/workspace"  # Path INSIDE the container (default: /)
461|#   timeout: 180
462|#   lifetime_seconds: 300
463|#   docker_image: "nousresearch/hermes-sandbox:desktop"
464|#   docker_mount_cwd_to_workspace: true   # Explicit opt-in: mount your launch cwd into /workspace
465|#   # Optional: run the container as your host user's uid:gid so files written
466|#   # into bind-mounted dirs are owned by you, not root. Drops SETUID/SETGID
467|#   # caps too since no gosu privilege drop is needed. Leave off if your
468|#   # chosen docker_image expects to start as root.
469|#   docker_run_as_host_user: true
470|#   # Optional: explicitly forward selected env vars into Docker.
471|#   # These values come from your current shell first, then ~/.hermes/.env.
472|#   # Warning: anything forwarded here is visible to commands run in the container.
473|#   docker_forward_env:
474|#     - "GITHUB_TOKEN"
475|#     - "NPM_TOKEN"
476|#   # Optional: extra flags passed verbatim to docker run (appended after security defaults).
477|#   # Useful for adding capabilities (e.g. apt installs needing SETUID) or custom options.
478|#   # Example: add a Linux capability not included by default
479|#   # docker_extra_args:
480|#   #   - "--cap-add"
481|#   #   - "SETUID"
482|
483|# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
484|# OPTION 4: Singularity/Apptainer container
485|# Commands run in a Singularity container (common in HPC environments)
486|# Great for: HPC clusters, shared compute environments
487|# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
488|# terminal:
489|#   backend: "singularity"
490|#   cwd: "/workspace"  # Path INSIDE the container (default: /root)
491|#   timeout: 180
492|#   lifetime_seconds: 300
493|#   singularity_image: "docker://nousresearch/hermes-sandbox:desktop"

531|# SUDO SUPPORT (works with ALL backends above)
532|# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
533|# Add sudo_password to any terminal config above to enable sudo commands.
534|# The password is piped via `sudo -S`. Works with local, ssh, docker, etc.
535|#
536|# SECURITY WARNING: Password stored in plaintext!
537|#
538|# INTERACTIVE PROMPT: If sudo_password is unset and the CLI is running,
539|# you'll be prompted to enter your password when sudo is needed:
540|# - 45-second timeout (auto-skips if no input)
541|# - Press Enter to skip (command fails gracefully)
542|# - Password is hidden while typing
543|# - Password is cached for the session
544|#
545|# EMPTY PASSWORDS: Setting sudo_password to an explicit empty string is different
546|# from leaving it unset. Hermes will try an empty password via `sudo -S` and
547|# will not open the interactive prompt. This is useful for passwordless sudo,
548|# Touch ID sudo setups, and environments where prompting is just noise.
549|#
550|# ALTERNATIVES:
551|# - SSH backend: Configure passwordless sudo on the remote server
552|# - Containers: Run as root inside the container (no sudo needed)
553|# - Local: Configure /etc/sudoers for specific commands
554|#
555|# Example (add to your terminal section):
556|#   sudo_password: "your-password-here"

599|browser:
600|  # Inactivity timeout in seconds - browser sessions are automatically closed

603|  # Let an authenticated browser extension register as the controller for an
604|  # existing Hermes session. Disabled by default. Local API registration also

608|

610|  # Increase for long pages (for example, documentation or financial reports),
611|  # or decrease to reduce context usage. Minimum: 1000; default: 15000
612|  # (same per-page budget as web_extract).
613|  # snapshot_threshold: 15000
614|
615|  # JavaScript evaluation guardrails (both default false). restrict_evaluate
616|  # opts into a denylist that blocks sensitive primitives (cookies, storage,
617|  # clipboard, network, form values) in browser_console(expression=...) — use
618|  # it when the agent drives a logged-in profile. allow_unsafe_evaluate is the
619|  # legacy override that switches the denylist back off even when restrict is on.
620|  # restrict_evaluate: false
621|  # allow_unsafe_evaluate: false

623|# =============================================================================
624|# Tool Loop Guardrails
625|# =============================================================================
626|# Soft warnings are enabled by default. They append guidance to repeated failed
627|# or non-progressing tool results but still let the tool execute. Hard stops stay
628|# opt-in for interactive CLI/TUI/Desktop/ACP sessions, but default on for unattended
629|# gateway/cron sessions where nobody is present to interrupt a model that
630|# ignores loop warnings.
631|tool_loop_guardrails:
632|  warnings_enabled: true
633|  hard_stop_enabled: false
634|  non_interactive_hard_stop_enabled: true
635|  warn_after:
636|    exact_failure: 2
637|    same_tool_failure: 3
638|    idempotent_no_progress: 2
639|  hard_stop_after:
640|    exact_failure: 5
641|    same_tool_failure: 8
642|    idempotent_no_progress: 5

644|# =============================================================================
645|# Context Compression (Auto-shrinks long conversations)
646|# =============================================================================
647|# When conversation approaches model's context limit, middle turns are
648|# automatically summarized to free up space while preserving important context.
649|#
650|# HOW IT WORKS:
651|# 1. Tracks actual token usage from API responses (not estimates)
652|# 2. When prompt_tokens >= threshold% of model's context_length, triggers compression
653|# 3. Protects first 3 turns (system prompt, initial request, first response)
654|# 4. Protects last N turns (default 20 messages = ~10 full turns of recent context)
655|# 5. Summarizes middle turns using a fast/cheap model
656|# 6. Inserts summary as a user message, continues conversation seamlessly
657|#
658|# Post-compression tail budget is target_ratio × threshold × context_length:
659|#   200K context, threshold 0.50, ratio 0.20 → 20K tokens of recent tail preserved
660|#   1M   context, threshold 0.50, ratio 0.20 → 100K tokens of recent tail preserved
661|#
662|compression:
663|  # Enable automatic context compression (default: true)
664|  # Set to false if you prefer to manage context manually or want errors on overflow
665|  enabled: true
666|
667|  # Fail closed before lossy compaction unless an active memory provider that
668|  # implements the pre-compress checkpoint contract (API v2) confirms its
669|  # durable checkpoint (default: false). With this on and no checkpoint, the
670|  # compaction attempt errors with BLOCKED_MISSING_PREREQUISITE and the
671|  # uncompressed transcript is preserved for a later retry. The gate binds to
672|  # every compaction authority: server-side native compaction
673|  # (codex_responses_native) is suppressed while armed, post-turn
674|  # micro-compaction is forced off (no checkpoint hook in its path), and the
675|  # codex_app_server API mode is refused at agent init (the codex agent
676|  # compacts its own thread — no checkpoint can be guaranteed there). Only
677|  # enable it with a checkpoint-capable provider configured — see
678|  # website/docs/developer-guide/memory-provider-plugin.md
679|  # ("Pre-Compress Checkpoints").
680|  checkpoint_required: false
681|
682|  # Opt-in compression progress notices on chat platforms (default: false).
683|  # By design, routine automatic compression is SILENT on human-facing chat
684|  # gateways (Telegram, Discord, Slack, ...) — it happens in the background
685|  # with server-side logging only. Set true to also deliver the routine
686|  # progress statuses (compacting started, preflight/pre-API compression,
687|  # idle compaction, retry progress, and the compaction-complete notice) to
688|  # chat platforms. Unrelated operational noise (auxiliary model failures,
689|  # provider retry chatter) stays suppressed either way, and compression
690|  # FAILURE notices + manual /compress feedback are always visible
691|  # regardless of this setting. (#52995)
692|  progress_notices: false
693|
694|  # Trigger compression at this % of model's context limit (default: 0.50 = 50%)
695|  # Lower values = more aggressive compression, higher values = compress later
696|  # Models with context windows below 512K are floored at 0.75 (raise-only) so
697|  # compaction doesn't fire with half the window still free; set above 0.75 to override.
698|  threshold: 0.50
699|
700|  # Per-model threshold overrides: keys are substring-matched against the model
701|  # name (longest match wins). Useful when some models need different compaction
702|  # points — e.g. a 1M-context model can compress later (0.30) while a 128K
703|  # model needs to compress earlier (0.60). The small-context floor (75% for
704|  # <512K models) still applies on top of per-model overrides.
705|  # model_thresholds:
706|  #   "glm-5.2": 0.40
707|  #   "claude-sonnet": 0.35
708|  #   "gpt-5": 0.30
709|
710|  # Optional absolute token cap for the compression trigger (default: null = disabled).
711|  # When set, compression fires at the LOWER of the ratio-based threshold and this
712|  # absolute token count. Clamped to the model's context length at apply-time, so a
713|  # cap above the window is a no-op. Survives model switches and fallback activations.
714|  # threshold_tokens: 200000
715|
716|  # Existing Codex gpt-5.5 behavior: raise Hermes' compaction trigger to 85%
717|  # for the ChatGPT Codex OAuth route. Set false to opt back down to threshold.
718|  codex_gpt55_autoraise: true
719|
720|  # Fraction of the threshold to preserve as recent tail (default: 0.20 = 20%)
721|  # e.g. 20% of 50% threshold = 10% of total context kept as recent messages.
722|  # Summary output is separately capped at 12K tokens (Gemini output limit).
723|  # Range: 0.10 - 0.80
724|  target_ratio: 0.20
725|
726|  # Number of most-recent messages to always preserve (default: 20 ≈ 10 full turns)
727|  # Higher values keep more recent conversation intact at the cost of more aggressive
728|  # compression of older turns.
729|  protect_last_n: 20
730|
731|  # Minimum number of REAL (actionable) user messages guaranteed to survive in
732|  # the uncompressed tail (default: 1 = the existing single last-user anchor,
733|  # behavior-preserving). Raise to e.g. 3 to keep the last 3 real user turns
734|  # verbatim even when bulky tool outputs fill the tail token budget — blank
735|  # platform echoes, compaction handoffs, and synthetic continuation rows never
736|  # count toward N. The tail can exceed the token budget when this pulls the
737|  # cut back; the guarantee wins over the budget by design.
738|  min_tail_user_messages: 1
739|
740|  # Compression retry rounds before a turn gives up with "max compression
741|  # attempts reached" (default: 3, same as the previous hardcoded value).
742|  # Raise (e.g. 6) for tool-schema-heavy sessions where 3 rounds cannot bring
743|  # the request estimate under the threshold. Validated >= 1, hard cap 10.
744|  max_attempts: 3
745|
746|  # Codex app-server (codex CLI runtime) thread-compaction mode. The codex
747|  # agent owns the real thread context on this runtime, so Hermes' summarizer
748|  # cannot shrink it — compaction goes through the app server instead.
749|  #   native = let Codex decide when to compact its own thread (default)
750|  #   hermes = let Hermes threshold trigger Codex thread/compact/start
751|  #   off    = Hermes will not auto-trigger compaction; Codex may still compact natively
752|  codex_app_server_auto: native
753|
754|  # Native OpenAI Responses server-side compaction (default: false). When true,
755|  # gpt-5.6-family models on the DIRECT OpenAI API (api.openai.com) or a ChatGPT
756|  # Codex subscription, plus gpt-6-astra (and its -900k alias) on official Codex OAuth, compact
757|  # server-side: OpenAI prunes older context into an
758|  # encrypted checkpoint that Hermes replays on later turns. No other provider,
759|  # route, or model is affected. Hermes' local compression stays armed as the
760|  # fallback and still handles every non-eligible session.
761|  codex_responses_native: false
762|
763|  # Optional absolute server compaction trigger in input tokens. The default
764|  # null value follows the resolved local compression trigger with an 8192 token
765|  # safety margin. For example, a local trigger of 765000 selects 756808.
766|  # A positive integer stays absolute and only clamps downward when needed so
767|  # the server compacts first. Invalid values use this automatic behavior. If
768|  # the local trigger is unavailable, automatic mode uses 200000.
769|  codex_responses_compact_threshold:
770|
771|  # Number of non-system messages to protect at the head of the transcript, in
772|  # ADDITION to the system prompt (which is always implicitly protected).
773|  # Head messages are NEVER summarized — they survive every compression
774|  # indefinitely. This gives stable early context for short/medium sessions,
775|  # but in long-running sessions that rely on rolling compaction the pinned
776|  # opening turns may not match how you want the session framed over time.
777|  # Set to 0 to preserve ONLY the system prompt (plus the rolling summary
778|  # and recent tail) — the cleanest configuration for long-running sessions.
779|  # Default 3 preserves the system prompt plus the first three non-system
780|  # head messages, matching the pre-feature behaviour.
781|  protect_first_n: 3
782|
783|  # Idle compaction (default: 0 = disabled). When > 0, a session that resumes
784|  # after at least this many seconds of inactivity compacts its accumulated
785|  # history up front, before the first reply, so a long-lived thread you come
786|  # back to later doesn't re-read its full stale context on every turn.
787|  # Time-based, so it complements (does not replace) the size-based `threshold`
788|  # above. It is skipped when the context is already small (at or below the
789|  # post-compression target = threshold × target_ratio), so it never wastes a
790|  # summarization on a short idle thread. Example: 1800 = compact after 30 min idle.
791|  idle_compact_after_seconds: 0
792|
793|  # Gateway session-hygiene turn-hold budget (default: 10). Max seconds an
794|  # arriving user turn is held while a still-streaming hygiene summary
795|  # finishes. Distinct from hygiene_timeout_seconds (compressor inactivity
796|  # budget): this bounds user-visible latency so chat transports (Telegram
797|  # ~30s) do not drop a silent connection. On expiry the turn proceeds
798|  # uncompressed; the detached worker keeps its commit admission (when the
799|  # commit is watermark-fenced) and the summary is adopted at the next safe
800|  # boundary. Thinking-model summarizers often need longer than 10s to emit
801|  # the first content token — raise to 300 (or >= your summarizer's real
802|  # time-to-first-content) only if you want THIS turn to wait for the
803|  # compression instead of adopting it one turn late.
804|  hygiene_max_turn_hold_seconds: 10
805|
806|  # Proactive tool-result prune (default: 0 = disabled). Opt-in token trigger
807|  # for a deterministic, no-LLM prune of OLD tool-result payloads, run
808|  # independently of `threshold` above. On large-window models (512K/1M) the
809|  # ratio threshold rarely fires, so bulky tool outputs (terminal dumps, file
810|  # reads, web extracts) ride along in history and get re-billed every turn.
811|  # When re-sent history exceeds this many tokens, the prune dedupes identical
812|  # results, summarizes older oversized ones, and truncates large tool-call
813|  # arguments — protecting the most recent `protect_last_n` messages and never
814|  # calling the model. Try 48000 to enable. Built-in compressor engine only;
815|  # other context engines inherit a safe no-op.
816|  # NOTE: a committed prune rewrites already-sent history, which invalidates
817|  # the provider's prompt-cache prefix — the min_reclaim gate below keeps
818|  # those cache breaks episodic (like a compression boundary) instead of
819|  # per-turn.
820|  proactive_prune_tokens: 0
821|
822|  # The prune's summarize pass only touches tool results larger than this many
823|  # characters (clamped to >= 200 so a generated summary can't be
824|  # re-summarized). Default 8000.
825|  proactive_prune_min_result_chars: 8000
826|
827|  # A proactive prune only COMMITS when it reclaims at least this many tokens
828|  # (measured on the pruned output). This is the prompt-cache hysteresis gate:
829|  # one meaningful, amortized cache break per batch of stale tool output
830|  # instead of a tiny break on every tool iteration. 0 = commit any non-zero
831|  # prune. Default 4096.
832|  proactive_prune_min_reclaim_tokens: 4096
833|
834|  # To pin a specific model/provider for compression summaries, use the
835|  # auxiliary section below (auxiliary.compression.provider / model).
836|
837|# =============================================================================
838|# Tool-result budget (optional)
839|# =============================================================================
840|# Controls when a large tool result is spilled to disk (full output saved to
841|# $HERMES_HOME/cache/spillover, preview + path kept in context). MCP tool
842|# results (tools named mcp_*) spill at a tighter 50,000-char threshold than
843|# the generic 100K default: MCP servers routinely return un-paginated 20-50K
844|# payloads that bloat context and slow every subsequent turn. Nothing is
845|# lost — the full result is on disk and readable with read_file.
846|#
847|# tool_budget:
848|#   mcp_result_size_chars: 50000   # per-result spillover threshold for mcp_* tools
849|
850|# =============================================================================
851|# Anthropic prompt caching TTL
852|# =============================================================================
853|# When prompt caching is active (Claude via OpenRouter or native Anthropic),
854|# Anthropic supports two TTL tiers for cached prefixes: "5m" (default) and
855|# "1h". Other values are ignored and "5m" is used.
856|#
857|prompt_caching:
858|  cache_ttl: "5m" # use "1h" for long sessions with pauses between turns
859|
860|# =============================================================================
861|# Auxiliary Models (Advanced — Experimental)
862|# =============================================================================
863|# Hermes uses lightweight "auxiliary" models for side tasks: image analysis,
864|# browser screenshot analysis, web page summarization, TTS audio-tag insertion,
865|# and context compression.
866|#
867|# By default these use Gemini Flash via OpenRouter or Nous Portal and are
868|# auto-detected from your credentials.  You do NOT need to change anything
869|# here for normal usage.
870|#
871|# WARNING: Overriding these with providers other than OpenRouter or Nous Portal
872|# is EXPERIMENTAL and may not work.  Not all models/providers support vision,
873|# produce usable summaries, or accept the same API format.  Change at your own
874|# risk — if things break, reset to "auto" / empty values.
875|#
876|# Each task has its own provider + model pair so you can mix providers.
877|# For example: OpenRouter for vision (needs multimodal), but your main
878|# local endpoint for compression (just needs text).
879|#
880|# Provider options:
881|#   "auto"       - Best available: OpenRouter → Nous Portal → main endpoint (default)
882|#   "openrouter" - Force OpenRouter (requires OPENROUTER_API_KEY)
883|#   "nous"       - Force Nous Portal (requires: hermes auth add nous)
884|#   "gemini"      - Force Google AI Studio direct (requires: GOOGLE_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY)
885|#   "ollama-cloud" - Ollama Cloud (requires: OLLAMA_API_KEY)
886|#   "codex"       - Force Codex OAuth (requires: hermes model → Codex).
887|#                  Uses gpt-5.3-codex which supports vision.
888|#   "main"       - Use your custom endpoint (OPENAI_BASE_URL + OPENAI_API_KEY).
889|#                  Works with OpenAI API, local models, or any OpenAI-compatible
890|#                  endpoint.  Also falls back to Codex OAuth and API-key providers.
891|#
892|# Model: leave empty to use the provider's default.  When empty, OpenRouter
893|# uses "google/gemini-3-flash-preview" and Nous uses "gemini-3-flash".
894|# Other providers pick a sensible default automatically.
895|#
896|# Native vision embeds (vision_analyze / browser screenshots when the MAIN model
897|# is vision-capable) ride conversation history and are re-sent on every later
898|# API call, so both knobs below bound recurring cost:
899|#
900|# vision:
901|#   # Byte budget for one embedded image (clamped 64 KiB..4 MiB). Raise it for
902|#   # dense phone screenshots of tables that read as "unreadable" at 256 KB.
903|#   embed_target_bytes: 262144
904|#   # How often vision_analyze may embed the SAME image (region crops included)
905|#   # per session. Unset = 3 inside delegated subagents, unlimited for the main
906|#   # agent; a number applies everywhere; 0 = unlimited.
907|#   max_calls_per_image: 3
908|#
909|# auxiliary:
910|#   # Image analysis: vision_analyze tool + browser screenshots
911|#   vision:
912|#     provider: "auto"
913|#     model: ""              # e.g. "google/gemini-2.5-flash", "openai/gpt-4o"
914|#     timeout: 30            # LLM API call timeout (seconds)
915|#     download_timeout: 30   # Image HTTP download timeout (seconds)
916|#                            # Increase for slow connections or self-hosted image servers
917|#     reasoning_effort: ""   # Per-task thinking level: none, minimal, low, medium,
918|#                            # high, xhigh, max, ultra. Empty = provider default.
919|#                            # Works on every auxiliary task block (vision,
920|#                            # web_extract, compression, title_generation, curator,
921|#                            # background_review, moa_reference, ...). Example: run
922|#                            # compression at "low" and vision at "none" to cut
923|#                            # side-task latency/cost on reasoning models.
924|#
925|#   # Web page scraping / summarization + browser page text extraction
926|#   web_extract:
927|#     provider: "auto"
928|#     model: ""
929|#     reasoning_effort: "low"
930|#
931|#   # Gemini 3.1 TTS hidden audio-tag insertion
932|#   tts_audio_tags:
933|#     provider: "auto"       # empty model = your main chat model
934|#     model: ""
935|#     timeout: 30
936|#
937|#   # Automatic session title generation after the first exchange
938|#   title_generation:
939|#     enabled: true          # set false to disable auto-title generation
940|#     model_upgrade_enabled: true  # set false to keep the instant derived title and skip the model call
941|#     provider: "auto"
942|#     model: ""
943|#     timeout: 30
944|#     language: ""           # empty = match the user's language; or e.g. "English"
945|#
946|#   # Session search — summarizes matching past sessions
947|#   session_search:
948|#     provider: "auto"
949|#     model: ""
950|#     timeout: 30
951|#     max_concurrency: 3    # Limit parallel summaries to reduce request-burst 429s
952|#     extra_body: {}        # Provider-specific OpenAI-compatible request fields
953|#                           # Example for providers that support request-body
954|#                           # reasoning controls:
955|#                           # extra_body:
956|#                           #   enable_thinking: false
957|#                           # Some vLLM/Qwen deployments expect this nested:
958|#                           # extra_body:
959|#                           #   chat_template_kwargs:
960|#                           #     enable_thinking: false
961|#
962|#   # Auto-generated short session titles after the first exchange.
963|#   # Each active Discord/Telegram channel can spawn a background title
964|#   # call.  Cap concurrency to keep retries during provider incidents
965|#   # from amplifying the request burst.  Leave unset for legacy behavior
966|#   # (unlimited).
967|#   title_generation:
968|#     provider: "auto"
969|#     model: ""
970|#     # max_concurrency: 2    # Optional: cap simultaneous title calls
971|#
972|#   # Context compression — summarizes long sessions to shrink the prompt.
973|#   # Heavy and often hits the slowest provider chain.  Setting a small
974|#   # cap prevents many sessions from compressing simultaneously during
975|#   # provider degradation.  Leave unset for legacy behavior (unlimited).
976|#   compression:
977|#     provider: "auto"
978|#     model: ""
979|#     # max_concurrency: 2    # Optional: cap simultaneous compression calls
980|#     # no_progress_timeout: 60   # Codex/Responses-only: seconds a stream may go without a
981|#                                 # substantive event before it fails fast (default: 60).
982|#                                 # Independent of "timeout" above (the overall request
983|#                                 # budget) — raising "timeout" alone does not widen this
984|#                                 # window. Each substantive event re-arms it; a slow but
985|#                                 # progressing reasoning/summary stream is not affected.
986|#
987|#   # Post-turn memory/skill self-improvement review fork. Runs after a turn
988|#   # when the nudge intervals fire; writes skills/memories in a daemon thread.
989|#   # Usage is recorded under session_model_usage task='background_review'.
990|#   background_review:
991|#     enabled: true            # false = skip automatic forks (/refine still works)
992|#     provider: "auto"         # or pin a cheaper model (see memory.md)
993|#     model: ""

995|# =============================================================================
996|# Persistent Memory
997|# =============================================================================
998|# Bounded curated memory injected into the system prompt every session.
999|# Two stores: MEMORY.md (agent's notes) and USER.md (user profile).
1000|# Character limits keep the memory small and focused. The agent manages
1001|# pruning -- when at the limit, it must consolidate or replace entries.
1002|# Disabled by default in batch_runner.
1003|#
1004|memory:
1005|  # Agent's personal notes: environment facts, conventions, things learned
1006|  memory_enabled: true
1007|
1008|  # User profile: preferences, communication style, expectations
1009|  user_profile_enabled: true
1010|
1011|  # Character limits (~2.75 chars per token, model-independent)
1012|  memory_char_limit: 2200   # ~800 tokens
1013|  user_char_limit: 1375     # ~500 tokens
1014|
1015|  # Periodic memory nudge: remind the agent to consider saving memories
1016|  # every N user turns. Set to 0 to disable. Only active when memory is enabled.
1017|  nudge_interval: 10        # Nudge every 10 user turns (0 = disabled)
1018|
1019|# =============================================================================
1020|# Session Continuity (Messaging Platforms)
1021|# =============================================================================
1022|# Conversations persist across inactivity and daily boundaries. Use /new or
1023|# /reset explicitly; context compression manages long conversations.
1024|
1025|# Maximum number of simultaneously active chat sessions across CLI, TUI,
1026|# dashboard chat, and messaging gateway. Set to null, 0, or omit to allow
1027|# unlimited concurrent sessions. When the limit is reached, new sessions get a
1028|# clean error while existing active sessions keep their normal behavior. This
1029|# top-level key takes precedence over gateway.max_concurrent_sessions. The cap
1030|# is a best-effort single-host/profile runtime guard; Hermes fails open if the
1031|# local runtime lease registry cannot be read or locked.
1032|max_concurrent_sessions:
1033|
1034|# When true, group/channel chats use one session per participant when the platform
1035|# provides a user ID. This is the secure default and prevents users in the same
1036|# room from sharing context, interrupts, and token costs. Set false only if you
1037|# explicitly want one shared "room brain" per group/channel.
1038|group_sessions_per_user: true
1039|
1040|# =============================================================================
1041|# Session Storage Retention (state.db)
1042|# =============================================================================
1043|# ~/.hermes/state.db keeps every session, message, and tool call, plus the
1044|# FTS5 search indexes. Since #54189, auto-pruning is ON by default so the file
1045|# stays bounded: at CLI/gateway/cron startup (at most once per
1046|# min_interval_hours) Hermes deletes ENDED sessions whose last activity is
1047|# older than retention_days. Open, pinned, and in-progress sessions are never
1048|# deleted. Stale automation sessions (cron/kanban/subagent/one-shot CLI) whose
1049|# process died without closing them are first *closed*, then aged through a
1050|# further full retention window before removal.
1051|#
1052|# After a prune that removed rows, VACUUM reclaims disk space only when both
1053|# the time throttle (min_vacuum_interval_days) has elapsed AND more than 25%
1054|# of the file's pages are reclaimable — a dense database never pays for a full
1055|# rewrite to reclaim a few MB.
1056|#
1057|# Uncomment to change the defaults shown; set auto_prune: false to keep every
1058|# ended session forever (the pre-#54189 behavior).
1059|# sessions:
1060|#   auto_prune: true
1061|#   retention_days: 90
1062|#   vacuum_after_prune: true
1063|#   min_vacuum_interval_days: 30
1064|#   min_interval_hours: 24
1065|
1066|# Optional direct endpoint for autonomous Bot Mode rooms spanning gateways.
1067|# Leave unset for the safe default: Desktop coordinates cross-gateway rooms and
1068|# same-gateway rooms can still continue on their own. Set this only to the
1069|# public HTTPS base URL that another trusted Hermes gateway can reach. The API
1070|# server key authorizes the initial invitation; scoped grants are signed by a
1071|# separate installation-private secret and survive API-key rotation. Disbanding
1072|# a Group Chat revokes its known peer routes; API-key rotation alone does not.
1073|# Network access should still be limited to the peer gateways (for example with
1074|# your VPN or firewall).
1075|# Plain HTTP is accepted only for loopback testing; every reachable peer URL
1076|# must use HTTPS.
1077|#
1078|# gateway:
1079|#   room_link_url: "https://hermes.example.net"
1080|#
1081|# The equivalent environment override is HERMES_ROOM_LINK_URL. After changing
1082|# it, restart the gateway and reopen New Group Chat > Advanced; Hermes will
1083|# re-check the selected gateways automatically.
1084|
1085|# Startup sweep of session rows orphaned by a dead gateway process.
1086|# The normal disconnect cleanup runs on an in-process grace timer, so a
1087|# gateway restart (update, crash, systemd) leaves those rows permanently
1088|# "active". On every gateway boot — stdio TUI *and* the desktop/dashboard
1089|# WS sidecar — tui/desktop/subagent rows whose start time AND newest
1090|# message are both older than the session TTL (HERMES_TUI_SESSION_TTL_S,
1091|# default 6h) are closed with end_reason "startup_orphan_reap".
1092|# Messaging-platform sessions (Telegram, Discord, ...) are never touched;
1093|# live in-memory sessions are excluded; swept sessions stay resumable.
1094|#
1095|# dashboard:
1096|#   startup_orphan_sweep: true
1097|
1098|# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1099|# API Server — per-client model routing
1100|# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1101|# Route different API clients to different models/providers on a single
1102|# Hermes deployment.  Clients choose a backend by sending a specific string
1103|# as the OpenAI ``model`` field.  Unmapped model values fall back to the
1104|# global model configured in the ``model:`` section above, and an explicit
1105|# session /model override always wins over a route.
1106|#
1107|# Configure via the ``platforms.api_server.extra.model_routes`` gateway
1108|# config block:
1109|#
1110|#   platforms:
1111|#     api_server:
1112|#       enabled: true
1113|#       extra:
1114|#         key: "your-api-server-secret"
1115|#         model_routes:
1116|#           # Xiaozhi clients send model="minimax-m2" → routed to MiniMax via OpenRouter
1117|#           minimax-m2:
1118|#             model: "minimax/minimax-m1"
1119|#             provider: "openrouter"          # optional — overrides global provider
1120|#             # api_key: "sk-..."             # optional — per-route UPSTREAM provider
1121|#             #                                 key (NOT caller auth; never logged)
1122|#             # base_url: "https://..."       # optional — per-route base URL
1123|#           # GPT clients keep their own alias
1124|#           gpt-5:
1125|#             model: "openai/gpt-5"
1126|#             provider: "openrouter"
1127|#
1128|# Configured aliases are automatically listed by GET /v1/models so clients
1129|# can discover them without manual coordination.  Caller authentication is
1130|# unchanged: every request still authenticates with the global API server
1131|# key (``extra.key`` / API_SERVER_KEY).
1132|
1133|# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1134|# Gateway Streaming
1135|# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1136|# Stream tokens to messaging platforms in real-time. The bot sends a message
1137|# on first token, then progressively edits it as more tokens arrive.
1138|# Disabled by default — enable to try the streaming UX on Telegram/Discord/Slack.
1139|# For Telegram, partial edits are sent as plain text and only the final edit uses MarkdownV2.
1140|streaming:
1141|  enabled: false
1142|  # transport: edit           # "edit" = progressive editMessageText
1143|  # edit_interval: 0.3        # seconds between message edits
1144|  # buffer_threshold: 40      # chars before forcing an edit flush
1145|  # cursor: " ▉"              # cursor shown during streaming
1146|
1147|# =============================================================================
1148|# Skills Configuration
1149|# =============================================================================
1150|# Skills are reusable procedures the agent can load and follow. The agent can
1151|# also create new skills after completing complex tasks.
1152|#
1153|skills:
1154|  # Nudge the agent to create skills after complex tasks.
1155|  # Every N tool-calling iterations, remind the model to consider saving a skill.
1156|  # Set to 0 to disable.
1157|  creation_nudge_interval: 15
1158|
1159|  # External skill directories — share skills across tools/agents without
1160|  # copying them into ~/.hermes/skills/.  Each path is expanded (~ and ${VAR})
1161|  # and resolved to an absolute path.  External dirs are read-only: skill
1162|  # creation always writes to ~/.hermes/skills/.  Local skills take precedence
1163|  # when names collide.
1164|  # external_dirs:
1165|  #   - ~/.agents/skills
1166|  #   - /home/shared/team-skills
1167|
1168|# =============================================================================
1169|# Agent Behavior
1170|# =============================================================================
1171|agent:
1172|  # Maximum tool-calling iterations per conversation (default: 500)
1173|  # Higher = more room for complex tasks, but costs more tokens
1174|  # Recommended: 20-30 for focused tasks, 50-100 for open exploration
1175|  max_turns: 500
1176|
1177|  # Inactivity timeout for gateway agent runs (seconds, 0 = unlimited).
1178|  # The agent can run indefinitely when actively calling tools or receiving
1179|  # API responses.  Only fires after the agent has been idle for this duration.
1180|  # gateway_timeout: 1800
1181|
1182|  # Maximum time an alias routing key waits for an active turn holding the same
1183|  # resolved session lease. On expiry Hermes rejects this inbound message and
1184|  # asks the user to resend rather than running it without serialization.
1185|  # Non-positive values fall back to the 5-second default.
1186|  # gateway_turn_lease_timeout: 5
1187|
1188|  # Staged warning: send a warning before escalating to full timeout.
1189|  # Fires once per run when inactivity reaches this threshold (seconds).
1190|  # Set to 0 to disable the warning.
1191|  # gateway_timeout_warning: 900
1192|
1193|  # Session stall watchdog (seconds). When a busy session has a pending
1194|  # inbound follow-up and the agent activity clock is idle this long, the
1195|  # gateway logs a WARNING and notifies the user to try /new. Does not kill
1196|  # the turn (see gateway_timeout). 0 = disable. Default 300.
1197|  # session_stall_timeout: 300
1198|
1199|  # Transcript-sanitiser repeated-heal escalation (#96870). The pre-send
1200|  # sanitiser silently repairs empty non-final turns on the wire copy; after
1201|  # this many heal passes within a 10-minute session window Hermes logs one
1202|  # ERROR (with session id + heal pattern) and sends a ONE-TIME out-of-band
1203|  # notice to the user suggesting /debug share or `hermes doctor`. The notice
1204|  # goes through the status channel only — conversation context and prompt
1205|  # caching are untouched. Set 0 to disable escalation (per-window WARNINGs
1206|  # still fire). Default 3.
1207|  # sanitizer_heal_escalation_threshold: 3
1208|
1209|  # Related in-agent compression timeouts (they live under the top-level
1210|  # compression: block, shown here for discoverability next to the stall
1211|  # watchdog they complement — a hung compression is a common stall cause):
1212|  # compression:
1213|  #   context_timeout_seconds: 120          # inactivity budget for in-agent
1214|  #                                         # compress_context (0 = disable)
1215|  #   context_total_ceiling_seconds: 600    # absolute cap on the pre-commit
1216|  #                                         # wait even while tokens stream
1217|
1218|  # Graceful drain timeout for gateway stop/restart (seconds).
1219|  # Default 0 = no drain: a restart interrupts in-flight agents immediately,
1220|  # cleans up, and exits. Set a positive value only if you want a grace
1221|  # window on /restart, and keep it well under systemd's TimeoutStopSec.
1222|  # restart_drain_timeout: 0
1223|
1224|  # Cron-only floor under the same drain (seconds). Default 30.
1225|  # restart_drain_timeout above is written for chat turns, which are cheap to
1226|  # interrupt: the user is told the gateway is restarting and the session
1227|  # resumes on their next message. A cron run has no such safety net — it is
1228|  # recorded in jobs.json as a permanent failure, nobody is waiting on it, and
1229|  # a recurring job simply skips to its next schedule. So in-flight cron work
1230|  # gets its own grace window instead of inheriting the 0 above.
1231|  # Clamped at runtime to the shutdown-watchdog leash (restart_drain_timeout
1232|  # + 60s) minus teardown headroom, so values past ~50s need a matching
1233|  # TimeoutStopSec bump to take effect. Set 0 to opt out and drain cron on
1234|  # restart_drain_timeout like before.
1235|  # cron_drain_timeout: 30
1236|
1237|  # In-band restart wait (seconds) for active turns to finish BEFORE stop()
1238|  # begins. /restart and SIGUSR1 refuse new work, then wait up to this cap for
1239|  # in-flight agent, cron and API runs to complete so the requesting turn is
1240|  # not cut off by restart_drain_timeout. 0 = enter stop()/drain immediately.
1241|  # The default (30 min) is a safety valve for wedged agents, not a target
1242|  # latency; raise it for long unattended turns. Env: HERMES_RESTART_AFTER_TURN_TIMEOUT.
1243|  # restart_after_turn_timeout: 1800
1244|
1245|  # Upper bound (seconds) a submitted prompt waits for the deferred agent
1246|  # build (MCP discovery, model metadata, skills scan) before failing with a
1247|  # visible error. The wait is patient — the message is delivered as soon as
1248|  # the build completes, and a progress notice is shown past 30s — so this cap
1249|  # only fires on a genuinely hung build. Raise it for deployments with many
1250|  # slow or unreachable MCP servers. Default 600.
1251|  # build_wait_timeout: 600
1252|
1253|  # Max app-level retry attempts for API errors (connection drops, provider
1254|  # timeouts, 5xx, etc.) before the agent surfaces the failure. Lower this
1255|  # to 1 if you use fallback providers and want fast failover on flaky
1256|  # primaries (default 3). The OpenAI SDK does its own low-level retries
1257|  # underneath this wrapper — this is the Hermes-level loop.
1258|  # api_max_retries: 3
1259|
1260|  # Once api_max_retries AND the fallback chain are spent on a transient outage
1261|  # (5xx, overloaded/529, connect/read timeouts) and nothing has been delivered
1262|  # yet, Hermes waits and retries this many more cycles (jittered 15/30/60/60/60s;
1263|  # a provider Retry-After wins, up to 120s) showing "Provider temporarily
1264|  # unavailable — retrying automatically in Ns (cycle k/5); press Esc to stop"
1265|  # instead of ending the turn. Auth/format/billing/policy errors never enter.
1266|  # Set 0 to disable (default 5).
1267|  # auto_recovery_cycles: 5
1268|
1269|  # After the agent edits code without fresh passing verification, nudge it to
1270|  # verify before finishing. Off by default (false). Set true to force it on
1271|  # everywhere, or "auto" for the surface-aware mode: on for interactive
1272|  # coding surfaces (CLI, TUI, desktop) and programmatic callers, off on
1273|  # conversational messaging surfaces (Telegram, Discord, etc.) where the
1274|  # verification summary would reach a human as chat noise. The
1275|  # HERMES_VERIFY_ON_STOP env var (1/0) takes precedence.
1276|  # verify_on_stop: false
1277|
1278|  # Standing operator instructions for the coding posture (when Hermes is in a
1279|  # code workspace). Appended to the coding brief as an extra system block, so
1280|  # you can pin project-wide workflow rules without editing the shipped brief.
1281|  # Accepts a string or a list of strings. Takes effect next session.
1282|  # coding_instructions:
1283|  #   - "For UI work, don't run tsc/lint until I approve the look."
1284|  #   - "Clean the diff before you commit and push."
1285|
1286|  # When verify-on-stop finds edited code without fresh verification evidence,
1287|  # append guidance for creative UI work (avoid broad tsc/lint/test before visual
1288|  # approval) and clean-diff expectations. Set false to keep that nudge terse.
1289|  # verify_guidance: true
1290|
1291|  # A `pre_verify` hook (plugin or shell, see Event Hooks docs) can keep the
1292|  # agent going one more turn to verify/clean before finishing. This caps how
1293|  # many times one turn may be nudged to continue, so a hook can't trap the loop.
1294|  # Default 3.
1295|  # max_verify_nudges: 3
1296|
1297|  # Enable verbose logging
1298|  verbose: false
1299|
1300|  # Reasoning effort level (OpenRouter and Nous Portal)
1301|  # Controls how much "thinking" the model does before responding.
1302|  # Options: "xhigh" (max), "high", "medium", "low", "minimal", "none" (disable)
1303|  # Providers with bespoke thinking tiers (a relay serving fast/thinking): use the

1305|  #   reasoning_effort:

1310|  # Per-model reasoning effort overrides (optional dict)
